question.text: A ball is dropped vertically from a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> above the ground. It hits the ground and bounces up vertically to a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo></math> Neglecting subsequent motion and air resistance, its velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> varies with height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> above the ground as

solution.text:

v2=u2±2gh
